newsitem.title: DENMARK: BG says to sell 40 pct of non-core production centres. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BG says to sell 40 pct of non-core production centres. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to make clear that company plans to sell 40 percent of non-core production centres and not upstream assets.)

COPENHAGEN, June 11, Reuter - BG plc's BG Exploration and Production will sell off 40 percent of its non-core production centres, but production will be unaffected -- balanced by new fields coming onstream, BG Managing Director Frank Chapman told Reuters here on Wednesday
Chapman said the cut would reduce production centres to just nine by February of next year.
"We hope to get it down to nine production centres producing revenue," said Chapman. "They will generate the cash flow necessary to finance the development of the rest of the portfolio."
He said that BG was not selling part of the portfolio to raise cash, but was "improving" it to eliminate assets which take a lot of time to manage but produce little return.

"The idea is to sell as many properties as possible without having a significant impact on the value or cash generative capability of the business," he said. But he would not be drawn on which assets were to be sold, or even on an exact number.

He added that production will not be affected as a result, as the company will start producing at an annual rate of 260 million cubic feet a day (mcfd) from 1 July from the North Sea's J-Block, now that a series of disputes with Enron have been resolved.
And the Armada field also comes onstream in October. These two assets will more than offset lost production, he said.

He said that the Exploration and Production (E+P) business, excluding the Morecambe fields which have now been given to Centrica plc as part of the demerger of British Gas plc, had never made a profit before.
He also identified a number of areas which he said would absorb the revenue generated under the portfolio improvement plan.

These included the Easington Catchment Area in the North Sea, the J-Block and Jade, Orion and Ross,the Elgin/Franklin development and Block 13/24, all in the North Sea; the North Coast Marine Area, an LNG project, in Trinidad; Rosetta in Egypt; Karachaganak in Kazakhstan, in which he said BG will shortly reduce its stake fom 42.5 percent to 32.5 percent by selling 10 percent to Texaco; Bongkot in Thailand ("the most prospective area in the portfolio"); and Muturi in Indonesia.
Chapman is convinced that the portfolio improvement project will enhance the company's share value.
Chapman said that valuing BG E+P within BG plc has caused difficulty to analysts, whose valuations have ranged from around 2.5 billion stg to over 4 billion stg.

Although he pointed out that such valuations reflected different methodologies, he believed the trend was positive, and said that E+P now accounted for around 40 percent of the overall market capitalisation of BG plc, "a big increase on the value assigned to it before."
BG has already pulled out of a number of countries, including Poland, Somalia, Yemen and Cambodia, and Chapman said they were now active in 12 countries.
Chapman said that an increase of two to three times current production in five years was "feasible," as was a return on capital employed of above 25 percent before tax.
